name: asymptote
why: A vector graphics language where diagrams are programmed mathematically, producing geometry from code in an unusual way.

brief.what_it_is: Asymptote is a descriptive vector graphics language for technical drawing, where figures are written as code in a mathematical coordinate framework. You feed it .asy source and it compiles the figure to vector output. Labels and equations are typeset with LaTeX. By default it produces PostScript, and it can also produce OpenGL, PDF, SVG, WebGL, V3D, and legacy PRC, plus any format ImageMagick can produce. The package includes the asy command and a rudimentary GUI called xasy for moving script-generated objects around, and a web application lets you try it without installing.
brief.why_it_exists: The manual presents it as a standard for typesetting mathematical figures, much as TeX/LaTeX is the de facto standard for equations, and says it was inspired by MetaPost but with a cleaner, C++-like syntax and more capability.
brief.how_it_works: Figures are compiled into virtual machine code for speed without sacrificing portability. Deferred drawing uses the simplex method to resolve size constraints between fixed-size objects such as labels and arrowheads and objects that should scale with the figure. Many features, including scientific graphing in the graph module, are written in Asymptote itself.
brief.install_notes: The manual has install sections for UNIX binary distributions, macOS binary distributions, Microsoft Windows, configuring, search paths, compiling from UNIX source, editing modes, Git, and uninstalling, but I did not open those pages, so no details beyond brew install are verified. The GUI xasy has its own installation section (13.1). The web application at asymptote.ualberta.ca runs without any install.
brief.standout: Figures are programmed mathematically, so you can do things like use complex multiplication to rotate a vector, and labels are real LaTeX typesetting. Its deferred drawing solves layout constraints between fixed-size labels and scaled geometry with a simplex solver, which is unusual for a drawing language.
brief.status: Appears maintained: the manual reports version 3.15-27 and copyright notices running through 2026. I did not find a release date or last-commit date, so this rests on the version and copyright lines alone.
brief.caveats: The homepage fetched as almost empty text, so the substance came from the manual pages. The manual describes xasy as rudimentary and says the GUI is still being developed into a fuller interface. The manual is licensed under the GNU LGPL. Build and install details for each platform were not read.
quotes: Asymptote is a powerful descriptive vector graphics language that provides a mathematical coordinate-based framework for technical drawing.
Labels and equations are typeset with LaTeX, for overall document consistency, yielding the same high level of typesetting quality that LaTeX provides for scientific text.
Asymptote is mathematically oriented (one can use complex multiplication to rotate a vector) and uses LaTeX to do the typesetting of labels.
